Both features come from @Henyckma.

A new Settings Presets screen provides six built-in profiles:

* Default
* Ultra Quality
* High Quality
* High Quality 30 FPS
* Performance
* Ultra Performance

Each preset shows which settings it changes. Device presets can provide an appropriate starting point, and configurations can be exported to a text file and imported again for sharing or moving between installs.

Emulation-Only Mode can release most of the frontend and optional services after a game has finished starting, leaving more of the device to the emulator.

Individual features can still be kept when needed, including patches, RetroAchievements, the OSD, Quick Menu and other optional services. Virtual controls are kept automatically when no external controller is connected.

The teardown process has also been made more reliable, including BIOS-only sessions.

## Performance and Frame Pacing

Frame-pacing settings have been reorganized into one panel instead of being spread across several screens and configuration keys.

Five presets are available:

* Optimal
* Smooth
* Low Latency
* Battery Saver
* Custom

They cover the frame limiter, FPS target, vsync queue depth, host-refresh synchronization and audio buffering.

Per-game settings use the same controls and allow individual values to fall back to **Use Global**. Applying a named preset per game also carries its FPS target with it.

Existing customized setups are preserved during migration rather than being replaced with a preset.

ARMSX2 also properly unlocks 120 Hz displays now, so ProMotion devices are no longer limited to 60 Hz by the app's own display configuration.

Several shared ARM performance paths have also been improved. GS vertex processing, MTVU synchronization and 16-bit graphics readbacks come from @bmdhacks; the FMV color conversion from @pstef; the compressed-disc caching from @jpolo1224.

Again, most measurements for this work were taken on ARM handheld hardware rather than iPhones. A few examples from that testing:

* On an SM6115 handheld, an MTVU synchronization change took Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 from 23.9 to 34.2 FPS in the tested workload.
* The updated NEON FMV color-conversion path took about 70% of the time of the previous version on Cortex-X1C and A78C cores.
* On an SD865 limited to 800 MHz, a native-resolution readback change reduced a 600-frame OutRun 2006 test from 16.2 ms to 15.4 ms per frame and also reduced run-to-run variation.

Compressed CHD images also have a larger decompressed-chunk cache, which helps games with seek patterns that repeatedly revisit recently read data.

## Graphics Fixes

Several long-standing graphics problems have been fixed.

### Apple GPU speckles

Small bright speckles could appear along triangle edges on Apple GPUs in games including Black and God of War II.

The problem came from differences between shader-written depth values and the values used by later fixed-function depth testing. The affected path is now avoided on Apple GPUs.

Against the software renderer, the problematic pixels in one God of War II Athena-statue test dropped from 220 to 1. A Black test dropped from 762 differing pixels to 2. Diagnosed and fixed by @bmdhacks.

### Dirge of Cerberus render passes

A new render-pass scheduler, also from @bmdhacks, can combine compatible hardware draws instead of opening a separate Metal pass for each one.

This is currently enabled only where the game database requests it. In a four-frame Dirge of Cerberus capture, the number of render passes fell from 8,035 to roughly 500.

Games that do not have this render-target pattern do not use the option.

### Texture-pool slowdown

A texture-pool aging bug could cause some scenes to become slow until a settings screen was opened. Texture aging now happens on every frame, including when duplicate frames are skipped. Found and fixed by @jpolo1224.

### iOS 17 startup crash

GPU enumeration used a Metal API that is only available on iOS 18 or later. On iOS 17 this could crash during graphics-device startup. The affected calls are now correctly version-gated.

### Replacement textures

If a replacement texture fails to upload, ARMSX2 now drops it and uses the game's original texture instead of continuing with invalid texture contents. This addresses cases such as missing cursors or partially drawn text in large replacement packs, and comes from @jpolo1224.

## Upscaling and Hardware-Fix Settings

Several problems made options such as **Align Sprite** appear to be stuck or ignored. These have been addressed together.

Graphics settings that can be applied while a game is running now reach the renderer correctly. The Renderer setting remains restart-only because changing it requires rebuilding the graphics device.

Changing a geometry-related hack also clears cached render targets where the previous adjustment may already have been baked into the image. This prevents old shifted geometry from remaining visible after a setting is disabled.

Game-database fixes can now be overridden per hack instead of requiring **Manual Hardware Fixes** to be enabled for everything. If you manually claim a setting such as Align Sprite, that choice overrides the database for that one option while the rest of the game's automatic fixes remain active.

The settings screen can also show the effective value currently used by the emulator and explain why it differs from the value you selected, such as a game-database override, automatic fix, per-game setting or 1x internal-resolution restriction.

One behavior has intentionally changed: manual hardware fixes are no longer applied to the BIOS screen or boot logo.

## Controller Skins and ARMSX2 Folder

Community controller skins can now be installed directly from **Browse Skins** in Virtual Pad settings.

The browser includes previews, author information, download sizes, search and refresh support. Download and installation errors are also reported more clearly. The catalogue itself is maintained by bagasromadon, and the skins in it by their individual authors.

Manual importing has been made more tolerant:

* Some malformed manifests containing stray control characters can now be repaired and read.
* Layouts that exist in a package but were omitted from its manifest can be detected automatically when the match is unambiguous.
* Re-importing an installed skin offers **Replace**, **Keep Both** or **Cancel** instead of silently creating a duplicate.
* Replacement imports preserve per-game skin and layout selections.
* Archives created on macOS no longer fail because of `__MACOSX` folders or `._` sidecar files.

You can also select an **ARMSX2 Folder** containing BIOS files, games, presets and skins. Access is remembered so the folder can be rescanned later, and newer versions of installed skin archives can be imported when the file on disk changes. The folder importer is @Henyckma's.

## RetroAchievements

The RetroAchievements panel now displays actual account and game information.

User statistics, current-game progress and the achievement list were previously connected to unimplemented core functions, leaving the panel empty. Those functions are implemented in 2.5.0.

Achievement notifications have also been moved to the native iOS toast system instead of going through an unused fullscreen overlay. Unlocks, mastery, leaderboard events, login messages and connection changes now appear through the native interface with the configured display duration.

A crash involving the lifetime of pending toast data has also been fixed. Thanks to @Henyckma for finding and fixing that one, and for the Hardcore automatic-fire restrictions described above.

## On-Screen Display

The OSD now respects the real UIKit safe area in each orientation.

Previously, the calculated safe-area information never reached the overlay, which could place top-right content too close to rounded corners or the Dynamic Island. Safe-area handling now works for the performance block and message toasts.

The performance overlay also shrinks when necessary so long lines remain on-screen after rotating to a narrower orientation.

Battery, thermal and memory information has returned to the overlay after being lost during the move to the shared core.

Rotating the device while the pause menu or per-game settings are open also updates those panels to the new orientation correctly.

## Stability and Correctness

2.5.0 contains a number of fixes that do not fit neatly into the sections above:

* A late signal during fallback from the iOS TXM JIT path can no longer kill the app during startup.
* An out-of-bounds read in the sprite-merge path has been fixed by @jpolo1224.
* A low-level iOS symbol collision affecting bundle-path and Metal-layer helpers has been corrected.
* PS2 shift amounts are now masked to the width used by the real hardware, fixing inconsistent behavior between the interpreter and recompilers and removing a possible out-of-bounds host read. Verified by @pstef against a probe run on a real console.
* The IOP interpreter now handles `jalr` correctly when the target and link registers are the same. Also @pstef.
* Per-game stick inversion settings opened from the library now load and save correctly even when no VM is running.
* **Reset All Overrides** now includes virtual-pad layout, controller skin and inversion settings.
* The Cheats and Patches screen now distinguishes between Hardcore Mode being selected and Hardcore actually being active, instead of claiming features are already blocked before a game has booted.

## Thanks

A large part of the core work in 2.5.0 came from the shared ARM development effort rather than from iOS-only changes, and most of what is new in the iOS app itself was written by @Henyckma.

@bmdhacks wrote the new recompiler family, the Apple GPU depth fixes, the render-pass scheduler, the GS vertex and MTVU work, and the move onto the shared game database.

@Henyckma wrote Dynamic Controls, the Dynamic Background system, Settings Presets, Emulation-Only Mode, the ARMSX2 Folder importer, the retained-tab and Liquid Glass navigation, the game-launch transition, and the RetroAchievements toast fix.

@pstef contributed the FMV color-conversion rewrite and two correctness fixes verified against real PS2 hardware. @jpolo1224 contributed the texture-pool, hardware-readback, sprite-merge, replacement-texture and CHD caching fixes. @XDarkFallenX contributed game-database corrections, and Mart's XMB recreation ships under the MIT licence.

And thanks to the testers who kept reporting the small things that were easy to dismiss as configuration problems. Several fixes in this release started with somebody demonstrating that a setting, game or screen really was behaving differently from what the emulator claimed.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.6
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.6

What's new: 

NASCAR Thunder 2002 fixed: cars rendered as shredded wireframes and would fall through the race track, or drive sideways. Fixed in the COP2 MADDA broadcast path. (@bmdhacks)

Dragon Quest VIII (PAL): hung forever on "Now checking memory cards (PS2)". The recompiler was merging a branch into a larger block when that branch's delay slot reads the EE timer, a read that must end the block instead. NTSC-U was unaffected only because its code sits at different addresses. 

8BitDo Pro and other Switch-mode pads fixed, holding R2 while moving the stick released the trigger, which made racing games unplayable. These pads report triggers as buttons rather than axes, and stick movement was overwriting the held trigger.

Display Resolution and Screen resolution override are now per-game. Changing them for one game no longer changes the global value. Existing settings carry over. 

Improvements for Macro buttons not accepting custom skins like every other button. (please let me know).

Improvements for separate landscape and portrait layouts in global settings, instead of one overwriting the other. (If you're still seeing a previous custom layout, just hit reset in the touch layout editor to see the new default layout for portrait mode, if you see overlap in landscape, do the same and hit reset. Remember you can make new profiles as well). 

Discord Rich Presence now shows your RetroAchievements progress, the game's own status line, unlocked count, and whether you're in Hardcore or Casual. (If a game has no Achievements, nothing will be shown for RPC). 

Added and updated cheats and patches for True Crime: New York City, ICO, Dog's Life, Primal, Stitch: Experiment 626 and Brave: The Search for Spirit Dancer. (@XDarkFallenX)

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.9
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5.9

What's new:

21:9 / ultrawide display mode. Available in Settings and in the in-game menu.

Screenshot is now an on-screen button. Enable SHOT in the touch layout editor
next to SAVE and LOAD. The core writes the PNG itself, so you get a clean
capture with no on-screen controls, OSD or letterboxing. 

Custom skins can now style the four macro buttons. Ship
ic_controller_macro1_button.png through macro4 in your skin (m1–m4 also works).
Combined with macros being bindable to any input, including L-Stick Left and
Right, you can build a proper racing layout: steer, steer, accelerate, brake.

Achievement notifications queue instead of arriving all at once. Finishing a
game submits every leaderboard in the same frame, which used to bury the
unlock you actually wanted to see under a wall of them. Three on screen at a
time now, and a queued one doesn't start counting down until it appears.

Fixed: the touch layout editor's grid showed buttons snapped while you dragged
them, then saved the unsnapped positions. It now saves what you saw.

Fixed: Vulkan failing to start entirely on some PowerVR devices (may help others as well) when the driver advertises a feature it doesn't actually support. It now checks
first and does without, rather than refusing to start the renderer at all.

Exit is back in the library's ⋮ menu, so quitting doesn't mean opening the
drawer and scrolling to the bottom. It remains in the drawer too.

Skins now sits next to Controls and Shortcuts in Settings.

Small improvements to controller navigation.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.8
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5.8

What's new:

Discord RPC is now built into ARMSX2. Link your Discord account from the Friends tab to show what you're playing, including each game's cover art while in-game and the ARMSX2 logo while browsing your library. The Friends tab shows which of your Discord friends are currently using ARMSX2, along with their avatar and the game they're playing. You'll also receive console-style notifications, in the library and in-game, when a friend starts using ARMSX2. A Friends button is available from the in-game menu, so you can check without leaving your game. The feature is completely opt-in and requires you to connect your Discord account. You can disconnect at any time. ARMSX2 does not create a separate account or operate an account or presence server for this feature. While connected, ARMSX2 sends Discord the title and disc serial of the game you're running plus its cover-art address, which appear on your Discord profile. Your Discord authorization token is stored locally in the app's private storage. Discord handles sign-in and processes the integration under its own terms and privacy policy. The Discord integration runs in a separate helper process and communicates with the emulator through a simple message interface. The GPL-covered emulator process never links against or loads Discord's proprietary SDK. When the feature is disabled, the helper process is not started and the Discord library is never loaded.

Added a What's New tab: read release notes in the app, with the people each release credits shown alongside it.

The game's CRC now appears next to its serial in the pause menu, in the
long-press game details, and once again in the Info tab, the two halves of a
<SERIAL>_<CRC>.pnach filename in one place. Thanks @Splaser.

Patch Manager: All on / All off for files with a lot of cheats, instead of
flipping a hundred switches by hand. Patch Manager also now shows the patches that ship inside ARMSX2 and apply to your game automatically. These were invisible before. A game could report "3 game patches are active" with an empty patch list and no way to find them. Patches with no name are always on by design, so there's a button to copy them into your own patches folder, where you can switch them off individually.

Fixed: pausing to change settings could crash with GS multithreading enabled.
Presenting a frame was the one path that didn't wait for the GS back thread, so
the settings you were changing were never actually the cause.

Fixed, in the texture pack manager: the screen freezing on large collections,
deleted packs coming back as "Installed", and games in your library not being
detected.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.7-1
releases.body:
Texture pack manager: Support for texture packs published in multiple parts. done by @sashkinbro

Wanted to get this out, but the team and I included need a break after the last few big updates we just had, I hope you guys take the time to enjoy and report feedback! Thanks. We will pick up again in a few days. Stay well!

releases.name: ARMX2 2.6.5.7
releases.body:
GS: fix missing draws on Adreno when texture replacements are loaded  done by @bmdhacks (fixes missing textures/textures not fully applying). Missing 2D text on Adreno with HD texture packs. Tales of the Abyss lost its entire text layer on Vulkan/Adreno with a pack loaded. Some draws read the render target while it's still bound as the color attachment, and Adreno silently drops them, a replacement texture shifts the source alpha range, which flips exactly those draws onto that path. Reading a separate copy is the only form that survives, confirmed on both Turnip and the proprietary driver. 

Also fixed in 2.6.5.6 hot fix, is Lego games crashing while using VK. Thanks! Will take a rest for a few days. enjoy.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.6 hot fix
releases.body: hotfix for Lego games crashing on vulkan

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.5
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5.5

What's new: 

Recompiler profile has been regenerated. The old PGO profile was generated for the old recompiler (pre 2.6.3). Offers a small performance boost.

Texture Preloading no longer silently drops to Partial. done by @sashkinbro

Portrait mode
The render no longer sits right under the camera. Portrait top-aligns the picture so the bottom stays free for touch controls, but it aligned flush to the window top directly beneath a punch-hole camera. 

Portrait has its own default pad layout now. There was only one default layout before, landscape-tuned, and portrait reused it.  Resetting a layout is per-orientation now too. 

3D covers render correctly in grid view. Two separate bugs, the slot was hardcoded to a 0.72 aspect for both styles, but 3D case renders are 0.646 against 2D scans' 0.696, so 3D art sat narrower than its slot with transparent margins each side. The grid also drew a persistent 1dp frame, which on a transparent 3D render traced a rectangle through empty space beside the artwork.

RetroAchievements sign-in now links to the website. There's no signup API, so anyone without an account had nowhere to go. 

Setup says "Next" rather than "Confirm", matching its own welcome copy. Back is a tonal button instead of bare text. 

Support for importing a cheats folder.

BIOS Folder import now carries .mec and .nvm.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.4
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5.4

What's new: 

Tidier UI. Fixes is now in the new Advanced tab, and absorbed the GameDB fixes from Performance plus the entire Recompiler tab. Both are debugging controls the GameDB already applies per game, so they don't belong in the tab you open to change speed. Fourteen tabs down to twelve. Search and the per-tab reset buttons moved with the settings, so searching "Skip MPEG" lands on Advanced, and resetting Performance no longer resets fixes it doesn't show.

Settings sections fold again. The collapse had silently stopped working, so every section in Pad, Renderer, Performance and Fixes was permanently open, twenty of them. It wasn't too many options, it was every option on screen at once. Sections now expand and collapse, and the state survives rotation. Renderer opens on Display & Resolution and Performance on Speedhacks so neither greets you with a wall of headers.

Fixed a bug when a replacement texture failed to upload to the GPU, it was still handed to the game with undefined contents, indistinguishable on screen from a texture that never loaded. Missing cursors and cut-off fonts on Vulkan were often this. Failed uploads now fall back to the original texture and say so in the log.

Skip BIOS is now on by default for fresh installs, existing users are not effected.

New texture packs download manager in the app. (done by @sashkinbro). Texture Packs now browses the community catalog maintained by @sashkinbro and installs with one tap. No game needs to be running. Each pack names the games it belongs to, so it installs itself to the right place, packs for games in your library sort to the top, and the rest stay visible so you can grab one before you own the disc. Texture replacement switches on automatically after an install, since it's off by default and the files would otherwise sit there changing nothing. Downloads are checksum-verified, check free space first, and swap into place atomically so a failed install never leaves you with a half-replaced pack. The panel links the catalog so you can see where packs come from and contribute your own. Be sure to read the contribution guidelines on the repo before doing so. https://github.com/sashkinbro/EmuCoreX-Textures 

The texture pack list collapses and is searchable, search by pack name, game, serial or author.

Per-driver GPU workarounds. (done by @sashkinbro). The GPU family was never enough to decide behaviour, the same Mali part behaves differently under ARM's driver than under Mesa. Driver identity, version and known defects now live in a 25-rule table with match confidence, so the next device-specific quirk is a table entry instead of another hand-written branch. Shaders gained swappable helpers for the bitwise operations some drivers miscompile. A device matching no rule renders exactly as before. An existing Mali fix was preserved and deliberately widened, Mali fixes reached through ANGLE or Panfrost previously fell outside it.

Your shader cache rebuilds once on first launch this update. Every shader's source changed, so the old cache can't be reused.

Library overflow menu trimmed from eleven rows to eight, with separators. 

Setup / Change Folders and Exit moved to the left side game library menu. Exit has a proper power icon and keeps its confirmation. 

Game names in grid moved to App settings beside cover size.

About moved to the left side game library menu. 

Installed patches and cheats can be collapsed, so a pnach with hundreds of downloaded codes folds away.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.3
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5.3

What's new:

Achievement progress now appears on every game that has achievements in List view, including ones you've never launched, a game with a set and no unlocks reads 0/40 rather than showing nothing. Hardcore and Casual are tracked separately. To enable it, go to the RetroAchievements panel in the game library --> Library progress --> paste your web API key (the panel links straight to the RA control panel login, the key is under "Applications" with a key symbol in the RA control panel). It then syncs itself once a day after the first time, or manually with the Sync library button. Progress also updates the moment an achievement unlocks, and is now recorded while you play whether or not you open the achievements panel. This feature is only available in the List View.

List layout now also  shows play time progress beside each game. 

New back up and restore option for the entire app. App tab --> Back up app data. One .zip holding save states, memory cards, cover art, per-game settings, controller profiles, cheats, patches, screenshots, and every preference, everything a fresh install destroys if using internal storage. Now you can restore your backups on fresh installs! (Custom folder users, you never had to worry about your data being wiped on uninstall to begin with). This should be most useful for Play users. 

Screenshot hotkey
Bindable to any controller button or stick direction. It captures the emulated frame at internal resolution no touch overlay, no OSD, no letterboxing, which is exactly what the system screenshot button can't give you. The PNG is saved to Pictures/ARMSX2 so it shows up in your gallery instead of hiding in app-private storage Android won't let you browse. 

Fixes: 

Serial and CRC without launching the game. Game Properties --> Info fills both in for any game. 

Patch import naming. Importing F0A6D880.txt produced F0A6D880.txt.pnach, which matched neither pattern the emulator searches, the patch listed as installed and could never load. Names are now built correctly, and the CRC is uppercased, since the emulator's file matching is case-sensitive and a lowercase name was just as invisible.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.2
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5.2 

What's new: 

Final Fantasy X: 10× less EE work. (done by @bmdhacks) Two recompiled blocks could invalidate each other and recompile forever. FFX (SLUS-20312) has such a pair at 0x002B9F48/0x002B9F5C. The EE thread was spending 95% of itself inside the recompiler and only 5% actually executing code, burning 51 MB of the 58 MB code cache every 48 frames. Over 300 frames: 9.6× fewer instructions, 10.7× fewer cycles.

Ad-masked blend fix: large win on tiler GPUs (like Mali!). (done by @bmdhacks) A destination-alpha blend with alpha writes masked was forcing an RT feedback read wherever framebuffer fetch existed. The read is cheap; the render pass isn't. NFS Underground was flipping it 697 times a frame against 40 real target switches.

passes/frame	frame time
Adreno 650	NFS Underground	440 --> 64	27.6 --> 7.6 ms
Adreno 650	FlatOut 2	954 --> 102	37.2 --> 16.4 ms
Mali-G52	NFS Underground	746 --> 69	276.6 --> 96.8 ms
Mali-G52	FlatOut 2	892 --> 96	373.6 --> 145.0 ms
Scored per-pixel against the software renderer, both GPUs came out more accurate.

Render-pass scheduler: new, off by default. (done by @bmdhacks) Queues draws and coalesces them across target alternations. Only helps games that ping-pong render targets. Worth testing in some GS heavy games. Measured over the dump corpus, frame hashes identical in both arms:

Dirge of Cerberus: 8035 --> 523 render passes. Enabled automatically via GameDB for all six regional serials; tested on an Adreno 650 handheld. "Coalesce render passes" in Renderer settings and the in-game menu. Toggle on and off to test.

VU1 flag packing rewritten for ARM64. (done by @bmdhacks) mVUupdateFlags was a literal x86 port, 16 instructions of flag packing around 2 instructions of real work, measuring 29% of all VU1 code time in God of War II. Now seven instructions. (GOW2 20% Speed boost!) 

EE and IOP stale-code fixes. (done by @bmdhacks) The block-invalidation walk stopped at the first non-overlapping neighbour, but blocks are ordered by start address, not end, so a longer block could be skipped and left executing stale code after self-modifying writes. 

Fixes: 

Fixed an issue with the emulator staying paused after closing the pause menu (FPS: N/A). The resume was scheduled on Compose's frame-callback dispatcher, so with nothing drawing it was never delivered.

Fixed a crash when changing settings from the pause menu. Android reclaims the idle audio device after a few seconds, and the reopen raced the emulator's own audio calls with no locking.

Audio no longer drops during a pause, returning from another app is immediate.

Fixed a permanent hang when backgrounded mid-frame.

Fixed an issue where the display was freezing for seconds after closing menus, an orientation flip was rebuilding the Vulkan swapchain twice.

Fixed an issue where settings written on one screen silently reverted by another.

Fixed an issue where Per-game Audio, Network and USB settings could not be cleared properly once set.

Fixed an issue with per-game settings not applying on Boot Disc / Swap Disc / BIOS launches.

Slowdowns in some scenes that "fixed themselves" when you changed any setting, the texture pool wasn't aged on frames that skipped presenting.

Save states: Failures now say why instead of closing as if saved, including the common case of the memory card being mid-write.

You no longer need to worry about texture-pack and patch import telling you to "boot a game first" right after quitting one.

Imported patches renamed to the form the core actually loads, and routed so widescreen patches aren't gated behind the cheats toggle.

Auto Progressive Scan doing nothing (Tekken 4, Criterion titles), the synthetic button hold was wiped by pad init during boot.

Frame Skip and Display FPS Cap work again, with FPS CAP: / SKIP: shown in the OSD.

Faster streaming in large games from compressed (.chd) images.

Dirge of Cerberus no longer needs hardware readbacks disabled. Renderer passes is now baked in for the game instead. 

New features: 

Fully transparent on-screen controls, support for 0% opacity, still touchable.

Block Home button while playing, optional screen pinning. 

Cover size slider for the library, in the App settings tab. 

New Pressure modifier slider amount, 5–95%, for DualShock 2 pressure-sensitive games.

7 new controller skins (by @bagasromadon), Midnight Club 3 Dub Edition, Kingdom Hearts 1 and 2 (+ JAPAN), Devil May Cry 3, Metal Gear Solid 3, Black Gold Solid, Black Gold Frosted

Long setting descriptions scroll instead of clipping.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5.1
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5.1

Crash & correctness fixes:

Fixed a crash when backgrounding the app during a game. Sending ARMSX2 to the background flushed the Vulkan pipeline cache from the UI thread while the graphics thread was still compiling shaders into it, a data race inside the GPU driver. This is the crash several people reported around pausing/opening the menu, and it hit Adreno and Xclipse alike. (If you still see a crash opening the menu via hotkey, please report it, that path is separate and may not be fixed.)

Fixed an out-of-bounds read in the sprite-merge path that could crash or corrupt rendering, a loop advanced the wrong variable and walked past the end of the vertex buffer.

Fixed NFS: Underground/Carbon-class hangs, the ARM64 FPU produced the wrong divide-by-zero constant, which let a game allocate a bogus 2-billion-entry table and wipe emulated memory (@bmdhacks). 

Fixed Xenosaga Episode 1 zoomed-in/half-black gameplay, a missing VU0 interlock on CTC2 --> vi00 (@bmdhacks).

Fixed stale recompiler links re-entering already-compiled code (@bmdhacks).

Fixed EE constant tracking being lost across memory-access boundaries (@bmdhacks).

Fixed a settings race where pausing could be missed because a flag was shared unsafely between threads.

Fixed settings silently doing nothing on games you'd used before. Per-game settings were stored in two places, and the older copy quietly overrode anything you changed from the library, permanently, for any setting it contained. It worked on fresh installs, which is why it went unnoticed. If a setting previously refused to stick on a particular game, try it again.

Fixed stale GPU shader/pipeline caches surviving an app update, which degraded performance until a clean reinstall.

Fixed screen rotation getting stuck. Two separate bugs: the BIOS ignored the Renderer page's rotation and always used the launcher's, and after exiting a game the launcher stayed locked in the game's orientation until you force-closed the app. Both are fixed, emulation and the launcher now have a proper split, and the cleanup runs on every path out of a game, not just one.

Three OpenGL correctness fixes: pixel-pack alignment is now restored after a GPU readback (a stale value could corrupt a later readback of a different format), a missing memory barrier was added after the CAS sharpening pass, and the depth-write shadow state now matches OpenGL's actual default instead of disagreeing with the driver on the first frame. Done by @sashkinbro

Performance: 

Async Hardware Download Mode (experimental, off by default), reads GPU data back without pausing emulation. Aimed at games that currently need a readback workaround, the data arrives a frame or two late. Done by @sashkinbro

Affinity Control Mode (experimental, off by default), choose which of the EE/VU/GS threads get the fastest CPU cores, or confine all three to the performance cluster.

Faster FMV/video decode (NEON rewrite), faster IOP code invalidation and memory stores, faster memory-fault lookups (@bmdhacks).

Texture-pack cache raised from 6 GB to 16 GB, so large packs stop evicting on high-RAM devices.

Local Link, play together over a local network (new):

Link two or more devices so games with a built-in LAN / System Link mode can play together, as if the consoles were wired to one switch. Roughly 57 PS2 games support it, including Gran Turismo 4, TimeSplitters 2, Midnight Club 3 and SOCOM, and there's a link to the full list in the Network tab. New Network modes: Online / Host local game / Join local game, Host shows its own address, guests just type it in, room code auto-generated peer IDs assigned automatically. Works over Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot, and over the internet if the host is reachable (via a VPN). Done by @sashkinbro (a tutorial for this will be present on our discord). 

Auto Progressive Scan (per-game), holds the button combo some games use to offer 480p. Done by @sashkinbro

New alternate OLED black setting that now combines with any accent colour, including Custom and RGB.

Added a toggle for use system keyboard, type with your phone's keyboard instead of the built-in one and vice versa.

Low Latency Mode is now off by default, existing installs are migrated once.

Game compatibility
Everybody's Golf 4 / Hot Shots Golf Fore! readback mode corrected across all regions (@XDarkFallenX).
Delta Force: Black Hawk Down, effect fixes (@XDarkFallenX).

Thank you to @pstef as well for PRing some of these fixes to @bmdhacks including faster video decode among many others mentioned in this change log.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.5
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.5

What's new:

Adreno GPUs now default to the Vulkan renderer when the renderer is set to Auto (faster on most Snapdragon devices). 

A new Low Latency frame pacing setting, now the default on capable devices, with a one-time migration so existing installs get it too (low-end devices keep the queued pacing).  Thank you to @Splaser for this feature!

Reduced Android input latency and improved input handling for controllers, thanks @Splaser 

Hardware ROV on mobile (experimental): the Rasterizer Order Views toggle now enables tile-native depth feedback (rasterization-order depth access) on supported mobile GPUs, (worth testing while upscaling). 

Added a New experimental CPU clock hint (ADPF) toggle in Performance settings (off by default). May be useful for low-end devices that are CPU bottlenecked.

Added open/close sound cues for pop-ups (info buttons, hardcore-mode toggle, patches & cheats dialogs).

Refreshed controller-navigation and slider sounds (I think these sound softer and nicer on the ears).

Delta Force: Black Hawk Down (SLUS-21124 / SLES-53299): GameDB fixes for correct effects, thanks @XDarkFallenX 

Updated the RA client. Stay on the latest version to keep hardcore mode working once the minimum client version is enforced (most likely sometime tomorrow).

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.9
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.4.9 

What's new:

Menu background colors, recolor the animated wave: XMB preset palette with 12 color options, a custom preset with RGB sliders, and an auto-cycling RGB mode. 

New menu sound effects, full UI SFX (and you can import-your-own or disable them if you'd like in the App tab of settings). Also included is sleep & wake chimes (like how the DS was back in the day) and a "Welcome Back!" banner when you come back to ARMSX2 from device sleep. 

Launcher rotation setting, orient the launcher independently of the in-game renderer. In the App tab of settings. 

Half-screen touch sticks option, whole left/right screen half acts as that analog stick. 

Quick save/load touch buttons,  tap now = current slot, long-press = picker.

Added back the option to export Memory Cards. 

Added Missables-only achievements filter.

Nightly-builds toggle in the updater.

Manual screen-resolution override (720p, 1080p, 1440p).

New settings are searchable.

Fixed:

"Missable" badge restored on rows + in-game.

Library music no longer dies when another app takes audio focus, and now returns after exiting a game.

App-updates section is controller-navigable now.

AYANEO controllers survive sleep/wake when using AYANEO controller mode instead of Xbox mode, and the right trigger works on non-standard axes. (let me know, I don't have an AYANEO device to test).

Rumble Racing sun-effect fix by @XDarkFallenX

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.8
releases.body: Test for check on launch auto updater.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.7
releases.body: Added a "Check on launch" toggle in the App-tab updater panel, off by default. Will automatically check for new versions to update on boot if enabled. (if you want to test out the check on launch feature, install 2.6.4.7 first manually, then enable the toggle and restart the app. It will prompt you to update to 2.6.4.8 on boot. Going forward you won't have to worry about this, only because this is new).

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.6
releases.body: Test for the auto updater.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.5
releases.body: Added an auto updater in the App tab of settings. It detects between stable and nightly releases depending on which version you are using, (and of course is GitHub only, Google Play updates on its own).

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.4
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.4.4 

RetroAchievements: Added a Locked/Unlocked filter with counts, notification and indicator settings (duration sliders + 3×3 position pickers for pop-ups and indicators).

Touch layout editor: Added a Grid option, and Snap-to-grid (buttons snap by centre), the settings panel is now movable & resizable, with resize buttons  (−/＋), remembered per landscape/portrait orientation.

Controls: Added a toggle in Settings --> Hotkeys, "Back button opens the menu". 

Mali-G615 (r44p1 driver): fixed a crash that took down effectively every game, a GPU “device lost” on both Vulkan *and* OpenGL. G615 users with a different driver were unaffected.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.3
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.4.3

What's new:

Dirge of Cerberus is fixed. It was crawling to the point of being unplayable before, and it now runs well (depends on device of course). Fixed by @bmdhacks. I noticed that with hardware readbacks disabled the game runs notably better, so while BMD works on further GS improvements, I've baked it in for this game. I also fixed hardware read back overrides not applying correctly for certain games, so games like Everybody's Golf 4 should have it baked in by default again.

2-3% EE speedup thanks to @bmdhacks 

Fixed an issue where Nintendo Joy-Con d-pad buttons would not map correctly or work in game. Now works as intended! 

Added a Fast-Forward Speed slider, right in the pause menu under Frame Limit. Pick how fast fast-forward runs, 2x up to 10x, or Unlimited (the default), so you can hold a steady 3x through a cutscene instead of blasting past the whole thing.

Added a Library opacity slider (Settings --> App). Fade the game rows and cards down so your wallpaper shows through the list instead of a wall of solid panels, or leave it at 100% for the look you have now.

Added the option to remove a single game from Recently Played. Long-press any game and pick "Remove from Recently Played" to drop just that one from the shelf without switching the whole row off, it comes back the next time you play it.

Fixed the game sometimes staying paused after you back out of the in-game menu, it resumes properly again now.

Added a warning for outdated cheats and patches in the patches and cheats menu.

Your recently-played list is also written to a plain file in your ARMSX2 folder now, so companion launchers can read what you've been playing. Thanks to @misantronic for this!

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.2
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.4.2

What's new:

Two new audio options under Settings --> Audio. OpenSL ES audio is a fallback
output path for devices where the default audio crackles, glitches or won't
start, it trades a little latency for compatibility, so leave it off unless you
need it. Lightweight audio skips the reverb processing to hand some CPU back to
low-end devices, you lose echo and reverb but get back a few frames, off by
default. Thank you to @sashkinbro for this feature.

Every GameDB Fix and Speedhack has its description back. The settings redesign
left most of those toggles blank with nothing telling you what they did, now
they all have proper descriptions again. 

Added a controller vibration strength slider (Settings --> Controls). This setting controls both touch control haptics and physical controller rumble, anywhere from 0% to 200%. Tame a motor that's too aggressive, or wake up one that's too weak.

Achievement sound volume: a slider under the RetroAchievements Sound Effects
toggle, so you can turn the unlock jingle down or up without going and editing
the sound file by hand.

Fixes to Per-game Reset actually resetting now. It was putting the on-screen values back but the game kept quietly running the old ones, so nothing really changed, it clears the real per-game config now, whether you hit Reset mid-game or from the library, and your patches and cheats stay put.

Fresh shader cache bump. 

Your RetroAchievements points show in the menu again even before you've loaded a game. They were read from the live client, which doesn't exist until a game
boots, now it falls back to the score cached when you signed in. Also added a user's RA profile picture and hardcore/softcore points in the RA in-game menu and full menu. 

Achievement sounds play with Do Not Disturb on. They were going out as a system
sound, which DND mutes, now they ride the game-audio channel, which it doesn't.

On-screen stats set to Custom now show the moment a game boots instead of hiding until you reset them, a new user's fresh install starts clean with the OSD off.

Audio no longer cuts out after the pause menu. Opening the
menu was pausing the audio stream and Android would quietly reclaim it while it
sat idle, it stays alive now so sound comes straight back when you close the menu.

Animated library background for the GPUs that can't run the live XMB wave. Older
Mali chips that were stuck with a still image get a moving backdrop instead,
everything that can run the real wave is unchanged.

A few GS/renderer fixes this round from @sashkinbro

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4.1
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.4.1

What's new:

Animated PlayStation-3 XMB library background. The library now has the live flowing XMB wave as its default backdrop, the way the iOS build does. Custom backgrounds still work, pick any image, GIF or WebP and it overrides the wave, reset returns to it.

On-screen stats hotkey now CYCLES instead of a plain on/off: Full --> Minimal --> Custom --> Off. The same modes are on the in-game On-Screen menu, and your choice is remembered. Hotkeys also are an option in the On-screen all settings tab.

Library music controls: a volume slider (now defaults to 15%), and you
can now pick your own track, any audio file from your device, with a reset-to-default. 

Display Zoom (Settings --> Fixes): one slider that zooms into the picture,
trimming every edge equally so it fills more of the screen without stretching
much simpler than the four manual crop sliders for tablets and modern screens.

Networking works again while fast-forwarding. 2.6.4 started handing the console public DNS servers it had to reach over a real network round-trip, which fast-forward outran, DNS now behaves as it did before.

Games no longer come back to a black screen (with audio) when relaunched on some Qualcomm Adreno devices. The Vulkan display surface is now rebuilt cleanly instead of getting stuck.

The replacement-texture cache was too small on higher-RAM devices and kept evicting a pack that would have fit it now scales to half of RAM (up to 6 GB instead of 2GB) so big packs stay usable.

Added more downloadable controller skins: Xbox, Burnout 3, Black, and more! 

Credits:

XMB background ported from linkev's
PlayStation-3-XMB. Controller skins by @bagasromadon.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.4
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.4

What's new:
 
Library music. The game library now plays an ambient track, like a console dashboard. It stops the moment a game boots, stays quiet if something else is already playing audio, and can be turned off in Settings --> App.

Download controller skins in-app. Settings --> Skins now browses the community skin repository with a preview image for each pack, and installs with one tap.

Added an On-screen keyboard hotkey. Bind a button to raise your device's keyboard over a running game and type into the emulated USB keyboard, for titles with in-game chat. Requires Emulate USB Keyboard ON in Network tab.

Added Play time and last played, shown in a game's Info tab. These totals have been recorded all along, just not exposed in the UI, so existing users already have hours waiting there.

More UI themes: Material You (Android 12+), an RGB rainbow cycle, a custom accent color picker, and Cyan, Orange, Red, Green, Pink, Purple, and more!

Shoulder buttons switch settings categories, for controller users.

Per-tab settings reset, so a single settings page can be restored to defaults without touching the rest.

Portrait: an option to align the display to the top of the screen rather than
centering it, now the default.

Achievements now show whether an achievement is an active challenge.

Fixes:

OpenGL (ANGLE) works again. Helpful for Mali and other low-end users. 

True Crime: New York City now fixed thanks to @bmdhacks (may have fixed LA as well).

OutRun 2006, Jak 3, and Jan X graphical issues (memcard hang still remains, restart game to bypass for the moment), fixed by @bmdhacks (more games may have been fixed as well from these improvements, as was seen in 2.6.3). 

Texture packs, fixed an out-of-memory crash on large packs, and heavy stutter as a
pack loads. The replacement-texture cache is now bounded and uploads are paced  across frames rather than landing in one.

DEV9 Ethernet, adapter selection and DNS now use the Android sockets path, so online play can find an adapter again. 

Patch enable state no longer bleeds between games, patches are scoped per game.

Folder memory cards on a custom data folder no longer crash, and improvements to per-game memory cards. 

Re added option to create Memory card folder. 

Joy-Con support! 

Saving or loading a state no longer leaves a black screen. 

Launching a .cue file from another app, such as Cocoon, should work again, (please let me know). 

The CRT/TV shader can be switched back off, selecting None now takes effect instead of leaving the previous shader running.

Adreno: the colorWriteMask-with-depth-test workaround no longer applies to Turnip drivers, which do not need it, thanks @bmdhacks 

EE FPU: MAX.S/MIN.S operands are clamped at clamp modes >= 1, and add/sub
guard-bit emulation is now unconditional, both bring the arm64 recompiler in line with the interpreter thanks to @bmdhacks 

Performance:

COP2 transfer ops now go through the register allocator instead of flushing everything unconditionally thanks to @bmdhacks 

The COP2 VU0-sync seam is outlined into shared stubs, shrinking generated code.
fastmem LQC2/SQC2 no longer emit an unconditional call flush. thanks to @bmdhacks 

Credits

Library music by The Cynic Project (CC0).

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.3
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.3 

What's new: 

New EE/VU recompiler backend done by @bmdhacks
The entire CPU core rebuilt on a new ARM64 recompiler ported from upstream PCSX2. Faster and far more accurate, a whole class of "unfixable on ARM" bugs are simply gone. Confirmed: Ratchet: Deadlocked graphical corruption fixed, and other problem games run as they should Crash Twinsanity, NFL 2K5, VP2 and the rest of the problem list now run correctly. This update should help low-end users greatly. 

GS Multi-threading (optional) by @bmdhacks
Splits GS onto a dedicated back thread, run 2x/3x internal resolution without the frame dips. Settings --> Renderer --> GS Multi-threading (and the in-game quick menu). Off by default, restart to apply.

Known issues, fixes being worked on:

Jak X: Combat Racing, slightly regressed (memory-card save hang + some in-game graphics glitches). Being worked on. For the moment, if you get stuck on it saving a memory card, restart the game and the save file will now exist. 

True Crime: New York City, fully regressed (the EE FPU accuracy fix isn't in the new backend yet). Being worked on, but I wanted to get this out now. Let us know how it is!

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.2
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.2 

Emulation Fixes: 

ESPN NFL 2K5 no longer freezes during early gameplay and now works as intended. 

Ratchet & Clank: Deadlocked, restored two COP2/VU0 sync fixes lost in the monorepo migration, plus a monotonic-clock guard that stopped the EE being slammed backwards. Game is now playable, although one graphical issue remains from my testing.

Folder memory cards work on a custom data folder again. Creating save data crashed or reported "format failed" for anyone whose data folder wasn't internal app storage. 

Texture Packs:

Importing a pack no longer freezes the app when using an SD card. A real pack is thousands of files over SAF, and the copy ran on the UI thread,  black screen, then "ARMSX2 isn't responding", worse on SD. Import and delete now run in the background with a live file count to let you know when it's completed. 

BC/DXT packs work on GPUs without hardware support. Devices that don't expose textureCompressionBC, Adreno 650-class hardware, and Mesa Turnip on any Adreno, silently dropped every texture in a pack. Those are now decoded on the CPU.

Texture Packs are now reachable in-game, from the pause menu, with a Restart Game to Apply button. Packs are only loaded at boot. 

The Texture Manager now shows which folder the emulator will actually read, and warns when no installed pack matches it. Booting a raw .ELF derives the folder name from the filename rather than the disc serial, which silently sent packs to a folder nothing scanned.

Memory card import now accepts folders instead of just zips of folders. Folder cards are directories, but the picker only accepted files, so a zipped card was renamed to .ps2 and read as unformatted. Folder cards can now be imported unpacked from a zip, with validation and a clear error instead of a bad card.

Settings & Behaviour:

Made more improvements to per-game settings, now apply when launching from a frontend (Cocoon, Daijisho, ES-DE). External launches passed no game identity, so every title fell back to global settings, including per-game memory cards and orientation.  (please report if this still misbehaves.)

Patches work with RetroAchievements Hardcore enabled again. Hardcore blocked all on-disk patch files in the new UI, while the bundled ones stayed active, so the same widescreen or bug-fix patch worked from our archive and silently died from disk. Cheats remain blocked.

Overscan Crop (Settings --> Fixes), trim pixels from any edge to hide garbage or black bars games leave in the area a CRT would have cut off. Measured in native pixels, so it behaves the same at any resolution. 

Custom OSD colours, including from the in-game menu. 

Support for Custom game names in the Info tab.

GameDB, merged community PRs from @XDarkFallenX

Rendering/perf fixes:

Marvel: Ultimate Alliance 1 & 2,  Everybody's Golf 4, Magna Carta: Tears of Blood, Rumble Racing, Atelier Iris 2 & 3, Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance 1 & 2, Jak 3, Kingdom Hearts II, Downhill Domination, Driv3r, Black, God Hand, Musashi: Samurai Legend, Aeon Flux, Artonelico: Melody of Elemia

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.1.3
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.1.3 

GameDB fixes: 

Synced all GameDB PRs from @XDarkFallenX which are Ratchet & Clank 2, RE Outbreak, Mark of Kri, Crazy Frog Racer, Grandia III, Grandia Xtreme, CoD Finest Hour, RE4, Tekken, Burnout 3, Genji, DOA2, Super Dragon Ball Z, Genji (SCPS-15095), DOA2 HARD. 

On-screen controls: 

Pause button replaces the settings cog. One clean ⏸ in the top-right, a single tap opens the pause menu. The cog is gone entirely.

"Tap to reveal" replaces the old show/hide toggle. When enabled, it's hidden-until-tapped (first tap surfaces it, second opens the menu) and the menu is always reachable, including with on-screen controls set to Never and after auto-hide. 

Interface: 

OSD now defaults to 65% (was 100%), the stats block was dominating handheld screens. Existing installs still on the old default are migrated once, custom sizes are preserved.

Fixed a mislabelled setting. The top slider in On-Screen read "UI Size (borders)" but actually drove the OSD scale, it and the real UI-size slider were sharing one label key. Renamed to "OSD Size" with its own description, and moved UI Size / UI Font Size up beside it so all three sizing controls are together.

Added a scroll-to-top button in Settings when scrolling through for example a huge list of cheats (like for GTA SA).

Patches: 

Patches now show up in per-game settings when fetching from the online browser.

Fixed cross-game patch bleed, opening GT4 could show GTA:SA's patches and cheats, in both the browser and per-game settings.

Improved UI lag on large cheat lists (collapsed sections no longer compose their rows). 

Patches and cheats have been split into separate collapsible sections when fetching them from the online browser.

Clarified widescreen patches, now "Auto-Apply Widescreen (16:9) Patches", with a description stating it applies automatically to every game that has one, and that non-16:9 titles can come out stretched, cropped, or missing text. It remains off by default. (I had it on and had the missing text issue in GT4, turned it off and GT4 was back to normal). 

RetroAchievements:

Added Encore, Spectator and Unofficial/Test modes.

Achievement sounds now actually ship so they can be further modified (unlock, message, leaderboard submit), the folder was previously empty. Unlock sounds can be configured through the app as before, the rest through the folder. 

Other: 

Potential fix for a Vulkan rendering regression on Snapdragon 8 Elite devices, (please let me know). 

Potential fix for an issue with texture packs not loading correctly and producing garbage data, (please let me know). 

Improved UI lagging after choosing a skin.

Per-game Graphics API, rotation and GPU driver are now per-game instead of global-only.

Load state menu slot tiles were squished due to the new Auto-save setting, they're now back to full size and should scale correctly. 

RetroArch shaders now render at display resolution. CRT scanlines and similar per-pixel effects were being generated at the internal resolution and then upscaled, which made them uneven. They now render at the on-screen size, matching RetroArch.

Per-orientation touch layout editing, editing landscape touch layout will not impact portrait touch layout and vice versa.

releases.name: ARMSX2 iOS 2.4.1
releases.body:
ARMSX2 iOS 2.4.1 is a much bigger follow-up than the version number might suggest.

This update adds video library backgrounds, MetalFX upscaling, more flexible controller and RetroAchievements settings, save-state previews, and a long list of interface improvements.

There has also been a lot of work under the hood. JIT handling is more resilient, several ARM64 and Metal paths have been improved, and a number of game-specific compatibility problems have been fixed.

Thank you to everyone who tested the builds, reported issues, and kept checking the fixes.

## Library backgrounds

Library backgrounds have been rebuilt around separate portrait and landscape slots.

Setting a portrait background no longer replaces the landscape one, or vice versa. Each slot clearly shows its orientation, file type, and size, so it is easier to see exactly what you are editing.

Each orientation also has its own fit mode:

* **Fill** fills the screen and crops the edges when necessary.
* **Fit** keeps the entire image visible and may add letterboxing.
* **Stretch** fills the screen by changing the image proportions.

Stretch mode has been fixed so it no longer leaves black bars along the sides in portrait or at the top and bottom in landscape.

Alongside static and animated images, the library can now use looping video backgrounds. MP4, MKV, and WebM files can be selected, and the player swaps cleanly when a different video is chosen. Videos resume properly after returning to the app and pause while ARMSX2 is in the background.

Background importing is also safer. A failed import can no longer remove or replace the background you were already using.

The dimming control now shows a live percentage, making it easier to use the same intensity across different backgrounds.

## Game cards

Portrait game cards finally receive the same frosted-glass treatment as their landscape versions. A subtle gradient behind the cards gives the glass something consistent to blur, while Reduce Transparency users receive an opaque fallback.

The cards themselves have received a small layout pass:

* Titles, file information, size, and region are centered beneath the cover.
* Additional padding gives the contents more breathing room.
* The favorite star has a lighter and less distracting background.
* The BIOS Only button is easier to notice.
* Favorite buttons in the list view have a larger and more reliable tap area.

## Save states and memory cards

Save states now display the screenshot captured with each state. This should make it much easier to recognise the point in the game you are about to restore.

Memory cards can be exported through the standard iOS share sheet. ZIP archives containing memory cards can also be imported directly into the app.

## Gameplay and controls

Portrait gameplay uses more of the available screen. The game viewport has been increased from 55% to 60% of the screen height, reducing the unused space between the game and the virtual controller.

The in-game pause button now uses a proper pause symbol instead of the previous ellipsis icon. The menu button also has better contrast, helping it remain visible over bright game scenes.

ARMSX2 now keeps the display awake while a game is running.

### Stick inversion

Each virtual stick axis can be inverted independently:

* Left stick horizontal
* Left stick vertical
* Right stick horizontal
* Right stick vertical

These options have global defaults and can also be overridden for individual games. The on-screen stick still follows your finger normally; only the input sent to the game is inverted.

### Rumble and haptics

When no rumble-capable physical controller is connected, PS2 rumble events can now be translated into iPhone haptic feedback.

This respects the existing Haptic Feedback setting and is rate-limited so sustained rumble does not overload the device’s haptic engine.

## Pause menu

Long game titles use end truncation instead of cutting text out of the middle, which keeps the beginning of the title readable.

The speed-control panel can also expand to full height. It should no longer remain stuck at half-height after rotating the device.

## Settings

The main Settings screen is no longer one long list of unrelated links. Options have been organised into five sections:

* Interface
* Emulation
* Input
* Storage & Memory
* Features

The JIT diagnostic panel has been moved below the main settings, so it is no longer the first thing most users see.

The BIOS list has also been cleaned up. Description text uses the normal interface font instead of monospaced text, and the empty state presents one clear action rather than two competing buttons.

A shader-cache reset option is now available from the app, making it easier to recover from a damaged or outdated cache without manually deleting files.

## Per-Game Settings

Per-Game Settings includes a new RetroAchievements category, allowing achievements and Hardcore Mode to be controlled for individual games.

The CPU section also exposes EE and IOP rounding and clamp modes for games that require more specific behaviour.

Messages about live settings have been corrected. Options that can apply immediately say so, while settings that need a restart no longer pretend to have changed instantly. The confirmation shown after saving also reflects what actually happened.

A bug that could create unwanted per-game cheat settings even when overrides were disabled has been fixed.

The panel background has been corrected in portrait, where it could previously appear as a flat black sheet. Warning styling and untranslated text have also been brought in line with the rest of the app.

## RetroAchievements

Expired or rejected RetroAchievements sessions are handled more clearly.

When stored login information is no longer valid, the settings screen shows "Not connected" and offers a "Log In Again" button. You no longer have to log out manually before being able to authenticate again.

Achievement notifications now queue properly. When several achievements unlock close together, their banners appear one after another instead of overlapping or replacing each other.

## Hardcore Mode and patches

Trusted widescreen and 60 FPS patches from the built-in patches database can now be used in Hardcore Mode. Cheats remain blocked.

The app checks where each patch came from rather than relying on its filename, so a cheat cannot bypass the restriction simply by being renamed to look like a 60 FPS patch.

Patch entries also show what is really happening:

* Hardcore-safe patches display a green check.
* Suppressed patches display an amber lock.
* A patch no longer appears enabled when Hardcore Mode has actually prevented it from running.

Turning a patch off while Hardcore Mode is active no longer permanently loses its previous selection. The selection is restored when Hardcore Mode is disabled.

Multiple patch and cheat databases are now merged while loading, improving coverage when more than one source is installed.

## MetalFX and graphics

MetalFX Spatial upscaling is now available on supported iPhones and iPads running iOS 16 or later.

It can be selected globally or for an individual game. Unsupported devices automatically fall back to the normal scaling path, with a one-time on-screen message explaining why MetalFX could not be used.

Several Metal rendering paths have also been cleaned up for Apple GPUs. Redundant desktop-style texture barriers are no longer used on iOS, and fixes have been made around framebuffer handling, texture-cache invalidation, downsampling, overlapping geometry, and feedback rendering.

The on-screen display has a new custom preset, and overlays should no longer be cut off near screen corners or rounded display edges.

## Audio and performance

The NEON-optimised SPU2 mixer is now active on iOS. Volume processing, voice accumulation, clamping, and parts of the reverb path can use ARM’s vector instructions, while the original scalar paths remain available as a fallback.

The ARM64 recompiler has received additional optimisations and correctness fixes, including immediate-value folding and improved handling for several floating-point operations.

Fast memory access has been hardened with safer address checks and fault handling. The frame limiter also reads the ARM64 hardware counter directly, reducing timing overhead.

Games that frequently read data back from the graphics system benefit from improvements to vertex submission and stall handling.

These are mostly internal changes, but together they should reduce unnecessary CPU and GPU work and avoid several correctness problems in affected games.

## Game compatibility

This release includes targeted GameDB, recompiler, and renderer fixes.

Notable changes include:

* **Ratchet: Deadlocked:** Fixed a VU0 and Emotion Engine timing deadlock that could leave the player invisible or the game stuck.
* **True Crime: New York City:** Added VU synchronisation fixes and removed a flag workaround that could cause graphical corruption.
* **Chaos Legion:** Added VU synchronisation fixes for affected scenes and menus.
* **Silent Hill 3:** Removed an outdated renderer workaround that could produce black FMV sequences.
* **Burnout 3:** The existing skybox correction is now applied on iOS. Made possible by @dr-sandwich
* **EyeToy games:** Fixed an iOS camera path that incorrectly referenced a desktop-only camera type.

A broader set of shared graphics fixes has also been pulled in for texture handling, framebuffer clears, flat shading, depth resizing, and other rendering edge cases.

## Stability

JIT handling has been made more resilient.

A startup watchdog also catches rare hangs while the emulator is preparing the virtual machine and displays an error instead of leaving the app indefinitely stuck on a black screen.

DEV9 HDD image paths are validated before use. If an image is missing or unsafe to open, DEV9 disables it cleanly rather than preventing the game from booting.

Malformed DDS texture replacements are also handled safely. Invalid texture dimensions can no longer request an enormous memory allocation and crash the app; the damaged texture is skipped instead.

## Accessibility and readability

VoiceOver coverage has been expanded across the game display, virtual controls, and performance HUD.

Battery level, thermal state, memory use, and Low Power Mode information can be read aloud without relying solely on the visual overlay.

Secondary text and frosted overlays have stronger contrast over bright game content. The secondary text color has been adjusted to meet the WCAG AA contrast target, and the background frost is more stable when the scene underneath changes rapidly.

Reduce Transparency continues to replace glass surfaces with solid alternatives where needed.

## Final note

Thank you again to the testing team.

There were a lot of small changes in this release, and many of them came directly from people repeatedly testing rough builds, checking fixes, and pointing out the parts of the app that still felt awkward.

That feedback made 2.4.1 a much more polished and reliable update.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.1.2
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.1.2 

Performance:

The Vulkan renderer now submits work mid-frame in games that read the GS back. Some games synchronously read graphics memory every frame, occlusion tests like sun glare are the common case, and that read has to wait for everything queued before it. Previously the GPU only started working at that point, so the frame became the CPU's recording time and the GPU's work back to back instead of side by side. Work is now submitted as it accumulates, so the GPU runs while the next commands are still being recorded and the read finds its results already waiting. Games that never read the GS back are unaffected, and nothing about what gets drawn changes. Thanks to @bmdhacks for this! 

Reapplied PGO, it had grown stale from numerous changes and needed to be rebuilt against the current code, making for a more optimized compiler. It had drifted far enough behind that the graphics code's hottest paths were being compiled with no profile at all, including the main draw function. Those paths are guided again.

Game titles:

Games now take their name from the game database rather than the filename, so titles are consistent and free of dump markers. Japanese releases show their actual Japanese titles, and sort by their kana reading rather than by character codes, which is what makes an alphabetized list mean anything in Japanese. There is an English titles option in the library menu for anyone who prefers romanized names, and search matches both, so a game listed in Japanese still answers to its English name. Titles refresh on the next library scan, so be sure to hit refresh in the game library if you don't yet see it.

Auto-save while playing:

Save states can now be written automatically at an interval you choose, from one to thirty minutes, so a crash or a flat battery costs at most that much progress. It writes the same auto-save slot the existing on-exit option uses, so your numbered slots stay your own and auto-load on boot picks it up unchanged. Off by default. Saving briefly pauses the game, so a short interval is noticeable, five minutes is a reasonable place to start.

Controller skins:

Skin packs that draw the left and right analog sticks differently now show both correctly. Previously the two stick images were treated as one, so whichever the pack listed second was drawn under both sticks, a pack marking its sticks L and R showed R on both. Packs that provide a single shared stick image, including the bundled ones, are unchanged. If you already imported an affected pack you will need to import it again, because the two images were merged as the pack was installed and only one of them was kept. This bug is now fixed. 

Interface scaling:

UI Size and UI Font Size in the On-Screen tab now do what they say. Both settings saved and restored correctly but were never applied to anything since the new UI change, so the sliders moved and the interface did not. They now scale the library, the pause menu and the settings screens. The game image and the on-screen touch controls are deliberately left alone, since the pad is positioned by your own touch layout and resizing it would move the buttons out from under your thumbs.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.1.1
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.1.1

What's new: 

Added modifiable Shader parameters, every RetroArch shader preset exposes its own settings, and you can now change them. Opening Shader Parameters brings up a full-screen editor: pick a parameter, adjust it, and watch the game change behind the list as you do. It works with a controller (D-pad to move and adjust) or by touch, and it handles the very large presets. There is a confirmation before going through with a reset. Reset all restores the preset's own defaults and asks first, because it can't be undone.

Once you've dialed a preset in, save it under a name with the on screen keyboard (works with a controller as well). It appears under My Presets in the Shader Preset list, so you can pick it any time, and set it for one game only like any other preset. Reopening it shows your values as its defaults, so Reset means back to what you saved. A saved preset points at the shader pack it was built from, so keep that pack installed.

Shader packs:

You can now install a pack you already have, from a folder or a .zip. Retro Crisis GDV-NTSC is available as a new download, it's a preset collection built on the RetroArch pack's shaders, so it installs into that pack and needs it first, and its entry stays disabled until then. The GitHub mirror of the main pack has been removed, it did not install reliably and the buildbot download is the one RetroArch itself uses.

Controller mapping profiles:

Save your button map, stick modes and stick binds under a name and pick it back later. A profile applies to the player and scope you're editing, so you can keep one map per game. Profiles are written to the inputprofiles folder alongside touch layouts, so they survive moving your data folder and can be shared. 

Per-game controller skins:

A game can have its own per-game controller skin now. Open a game's settings, turn on Use a different skin for this game, and pick one, every other game keeps what you had. Skins are also reachable from the in-game menu now, next to the touch layout editor in the controller tab.

Macros:

Added more Macros, can fire the D-pad, the analog toggle, the pressure modifier and either stick's directions, not just the face and shoulder buttons. Each macro also has a Frequency: leave it on Hold for the old behaviour, or set an interval to turn it into a turbo that toggles while held.

Fixes:

Patch and cheat settings now follow the Global and Per-Game switch. That page always read and wrote global settings regardless of the switch, so a setting meant for one game was saved for every game, and the in-game menu's patch rows, which did respect the switch, contradicted it.

A per-game setting now stays with the game once you set it. Previously a per-game value that happened to match the global one was not recorded, so later changing the global setting silently changed it for that game too. Settings you never touched for a game still follow the global one.

Launching from a front-end such as Cocoon or iiSU for example now shows the Global and Per-Game switch, and saves to the tier it says. Previously the game had no identity in the app, so the switch was missing while settings were still saved per game.

Touch profile lists scroll. Past four profiles the rest were pushed off the screen and could not be reached, which looked like a limit. Nothing was ever limited, but more than four profiles would get blocked off from view.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.1
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.1 

What's new:

Added RetroArch shaders, ARMSX2 now runs RetroArch .slangp shader chains on both Vulkan and OpenGL/GLES, via librashader. Download shader packs directly in-app, the same way GPU drivers already work, and pick a preset from Settings --> Renderer ---> Shader Preset once you've enabled RetroArch Shaders, you can also access it from the in-game menu without leaving your game. Preset changes apply live.

Presets are grouped by family (Mega Bezel, koko-aio, CRT, Handheld, and so on), collapsed by default, with each family split by its own folders so nothing stalls when you open the picker. Every preset shows its pass count as information, that number is not a performance prediction, and we deliberately don't rank presets by it: xBRZ runs heavy at ~5 passes, while koko-aio's ambilight runs great at ~19, because cost depends on per-pass resolution and shader complexity rather than pass count.

Fixes:

Add to home screen never actually pinned anything. The launcher was rejecting the full-size cover art as a shortcut icon, the error was being swallowed, and a legacy fallback that Android has ignored since 8.0 reported success, so even the failure toast never appeared. Icons are now scaled correctly and real failures surface.

Audio stayed muted after leaving the in-game menu open for a while, once Android reclaimed the audio stream. It now reopens on resume.

Added Force Framebuffer Fetch (MediaTek Mali), which is off by default. For Mali users on Vulkan only.
Off (default): correct picture, slower.
On: faster, but some MediaTek drivers show black or missing textures, will vary by device.

Added Gyro hotkeys, bind Gyro On/Off (toggle) and Gyro (hold to aim) to any button. Toggle flips gyro aiming on and off, hold enables it only while the button is held, so you can leave gyro out of the way until you're actually aiming. 

Exit to Launcher now actually exits to your launcher. With "Exit to Launcher on Close (External Games)" enabled, quitting a game you launched from ES-DE or another frontend returns you to that frontend, instead of dropping you into the ARMSX2 library.

Other

Added three About sections in the left bar menu with Discord, GitHub and Website links.

### Credits

RetroArch shader support in ARMSX2 stands entirely on other people's work:

**[librashader](https://github.com/SnowflakePowered/librashader)** by
  SnowflakePowered, the runtime that compiles and executes the shader
  chains on both Vulkan and OpenGL. 

**[libretro / RetroArch](https://github.com/libretro/RetroArch)** the
  `.slangp` preset format and the [slang-shaders](https://github.com/libretro/slang-shaders) collection.
  Shader packs are downloaded from the libretro buildbot, nothing is bundled
  with ARMSX2.

**The shader authors.** Every preset is someone's craft, and the good ones
  represent years of it, among many others: **HyperspaceMadness**
  (Mega Bezel), **kokoko3k** (koko-aio), **TroggleMonkey** (crt-royale),
  **Themaister** (the slang shader spec and many core shaders), **Hyllian**
  (xBR family), **guest.r**, **Lottes**, **cgwg** (crt-geom).
  Each preset carries its own licence and author in its `.slangp`/`.slang`
  files. 

If you maintain a shader pack and I've credited you wrongly or missed you,
please open an issue and I'll fix it.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.0.5
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.0.5 

What's new: 

Gyro + stick now work together. Aim gyro (and steering gyro) is now added on top of the physical stick instead of fighting it, use the right stick for coarse aim and tilt to fine-tune, both at once. The other stick (movement) is unaffected while you aim.

Fixed: per-game stick fixes leaked to every game. Right/Left Stick Invert X/Y, Swap X/Y, and D-pad as Left Stick now save per game when set in a game's properties (they were writing the global setting for all games).

Added Per-game BIOS option. Long-press a game --> Per-game BIOS button to boot that specific game with its own BIOS (like for a EU disc on a EU BIOS, a US disc on a US BIOS). Global BIOS is the default you choose, "Use global" reverts it.

Online patches now work from the library. The patch/cheat browser reads the game's serial straight from the disc, so you can browse and install patches from a game's per-game settings without booting it first (previously it only worked in-game).

ANGLE is now an OpenGL driver option. When you select the OpenGL renderer, the driver picker shows an ANGLE option (GLES-on-Vulkan), the OpenGL counterpart to the Vulkan driver list. Helps non-Adreno GPUs (Mali/Xclipse/PowerVR) whose native OpenGL driver is weak. Available in both the Renderer settings and the in-game Graphics menu.

New GPU driver source: ExynosTools (WearyConcern1165/ExynosTools) added to the in-app driver downloader, helps Xclipse devices on Vulkan.

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.6.0.4
releases.body:
ARMSX2 2.6.0.4

What's new:
